Quick update: we pulled edge DNS server logs (see Drive link) and proxy logs for the nodes hitting NXDOMAINs. I see a batch of requests being directed at an old internal resolver that FastRetail deprecated last week — there's a mismatch in the recent peering ACL that is sending traffic through a legacy proxy cluster with a much tighter connection timeout. That cluster is dropping long-running responses and causing 502s.

Plan (short):
- Stand up a temporary route to forward FastRetail egress to the healthy resolver cluster (fast path) — ETA 25min
- Patch proxy timeout to 90s on the legacy cluster to avoid mid-request termination — ETA 40min
- Collect pcap traces and reopen PD-87422

I will not do the route change without ops approval from FastRetail; tagging Jane to confirm.

Attachments added to Drive: signed-mop.pdf (proposed maintenance and explicit approval doc).

Ben
Escalations Lead, Redwood Inference

Jane / Hannah / Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for working through this quickly. Quick executive summary for FastRetail leadership:

- Impact: Production inference traffic experienced increased error rate (502/504) and elevated latency p95 from ~130ms to ~1.2s for a ~6 minute window during FastRetail's ASN migration (08:10–08:16 PST).
- Root cause: transient routing advertisement routed a subset of traffic through a deprecated resolver and legacy proxy cluster that had a lower connection timeout and was terminating in-flight responses.
- Mitigations applied: temporary fast-path route from Redwood to healthy resolver cluster (10:28 PST), proxy timeout patch on legacy cluster (11:05 PST).
- Current status: mitigated; small residual 502s observed while FastRetail purges deprecated peer from their peering ACLs.
- Actions: 1) Formal RCA draft (Marissa) by EOD 2028-02-15; 2) Permanent peering cleanup with FastRetail scheduled (work item); 3) Add ASN-swap canary checks to avoid future accidental advertisements.

We will send a short exec note for your leadership and coordinate a 30-minute Sync to align on the permanent fix next week.

Vivek Kulkarni
